correctness.rationale: The secant gain representation is exact for each pair of solutions. A mean-damping integrating factor and diagonal gain balance give theta_prime=d cos^2(theta)+c sin^2(theta)+delta sin(2theta), bounded by Omega+delta sin(2theta). Every coordinate equality is transverse. When |delta|<Omega, integrating the reciprocal majorant over one half-turn proves the universal pi/sqrt(Omega^2-delta^2) gap; at |delta|>=Omega a scalar barrier precludes the next half-turn. Explicit bounded strictly monotone C1 responses coincide with the critical affine system in a small invariant neighborhood, attaining the gap. The independent finite checker exercises exact coefficients, numerical angle integrals, and time-dependent secants without replacing the proof.

value.rationale: A natural projected trajectory-identification problem in inhibitory gene feedback acquires a complete sharp qualitative transition at |gamma1-gamma2|=2sqrt(AB), separating arbitrarily many possible first-output coincidences (with a sharp universal minimum gap) from at-most-one coincidence. This bound is robust under all admissible nonlinear gain profiles, identifies an exact observability-spacing limit and sharp bounded-response examples; it is more than a renaming of the equal-decay formula.
